text:
The Blackhawks lost Connor Bedard again and then started winning. Bedard hurt his right shoulder in mid-November, his third shoulder injury in less than a year, and has had surgery that Flames Nation's notebook says will keep him out four months. Since then Chicago has won four straight, the last a 2-1 win over the Rangers in front of 20,302, the biggest crowd of the season according to Scott Powers of The Athletic.

The young players are the story. Sam Rinzel has 14 points in his last 10 games and was named the NHL's third star of the week; Roman Kantserov, whose first career hat trick beat Vancouver, has 11. Both are running ahead of their chances (6.1 and 7.9 expected points), so enjoy it, but don't bank it.

The streak itself leans on Spencer Knight, who is .933 with 4.2 goals saved above expected over his last five starts. Chicago got only 48% of the expected goals during the run and 43.5% on the season, among the weakest in the league. Wyatt Kaiser's three-game suspension for a head hit also takes out half of a pair that has been outscored 15-4.

Our numbers give Chicago about a 1% chance at the playoffs, which is honest about the hole. Jeff Blashill's team is playing for something else this winter. What we'd watch: whether Rinzel and Kantserov keep producing once the shooting cools, and whether Knight gets the net for good while Arvid Soderblom struggles.
